Subject: Post-call: Long-context evals & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap + recommended next steps so we have alignment: 

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: evaluate model fidelity on extremely long customer support threads (50k-150k tokens) with reliable summarization and low truncation hallucinations.
- Success criteria: summary fidelity (human-rated) >= 90% on key entities, hallucination rate < 2% on sampled set, acceptable latency (< 2s per 1k tokens preview for interactive flows).

Redwood recommendation (short):
- Run a 1-week long-context eval using our rw_long-3.2 and rw_llama-65b-extended-q4 variants. Start with rw_long-3.2 (extended context) as the baseline.
- Eval dataset: 200 threads (sampled across your product/region mix). We'll test truncation behavior, summarization fidelity, and extractive QA performance.
- Prompt set: attached promptset + a small script to reproduce evaluation locally/remote.

Attachments / links:
- long-context-eval-promptset.jsonl (attached)
- initial-benchmarks.csv (attached)
- Shared folder with longer docs / S3 link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-long-context-eval

Next steps (suggested):
1) You share the sample dataset (S3/Drive) and confirm which 200 threads to include (action: Acme).
2) We provision a short pilot on Redwood Dedicated (1 GPU pool) and run the eval. (action: Redwood)
3) We review results and propose configuration (model variant, quantization, KV cache settings), then discuss pilot pricing and SLA. (action: both)

Do you want us to include your security contact in the thread for SOC2/questions?

I'll follow up with a proposed evaluation plan and an initial config matrix tomorrow.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: Long-context evals & next steps

Samir — great questions, answers below and a proposed config matrix attached. Looping Stephanie (Customer Success) and Dev (Solutions) to prep infra/procurement next steps.

On truncation / long-context handling:
- rw_long-3.2 supports native extended contexts up to ~200k tokens for inference when using dedicated nodes + KV cache. For your 120k-token threads we recommend:
  * Primary path: full-context decoding (native long model) to avoid sliding-window merge artifacts. This keeps entity integrity and reduces stitching hallucinations.
  * Fallback: for the rare >200k cases, use prefix-preserve + sliding window with overlap 2k tokens and entity-preserve heuristics.

On summarization fidelity & evaluation rubric:
- We'll run both automated metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore) and human evaluation (3 raters per summary, majority vote). We'll share the rubric and a short labeling guide (attached). Target: >=90% human-rated fidelity on core entities; hallucination rate <2% on sampled set.

On pilot cost estimate (rough):
- 1-week Dedicated pilot (2x dedicated GPUs configured for long-context ops) + storage & egress: estimated $12k–18k depending on throughput and retention. We can tighten this after we see the actual request distribution.

Attachments included: redwood-model-recommendation.pdf, eval-rubric.md, updated-benchmarks.csv

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Acme: confirm dataset S3 link + any redaction needs.
2) Redwood: provision pilot environment (Dev/Infra to confirm).
3) Kickoff call next Tues to align on labeling schedule — I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — we'll move quickly on this.

Best,
Marissa
